recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future Condition.asserter or Condition.recorder clarification should be handled through the later Patient Care issue family rather than reapplying the exact DSTU1 wording from FHIR-7855.
issue_request: FHIR-7855 was a Published Patient Care core Condition clarification from the DSTU1 ballot. It rejected the proposed wording that would make the asserter the person who recorded the condition, instead requiring the definition "Individual who is making the condition statement" and a usage note explaining that a separate data enterer can be represented with Provenance pointing to the Condition.
initial_application: Historical commit c6b154ca1b0087117ef7b89610c4e862b5357af9 (#7615, #7855, #7859) changed the old Condition spreadsheet asserter definition to "Individual who is making the condition statement." The required Provenance guidance is present in condition-notes.xml and traces to the same DSTU1-era Condition notes work.
additional_context: Condition is active in source/fhir.ini. Later core decisions explain current wording differences: FHIR-22270 added Device support and changed the asserter definition to "Individual or device that is making the condition statement"; FHIR-39602 restored explicit Condition.recorder and Condition.asserter after the R5 participant pattern; FHIR-41403 added Group targets; and FHIR-48804 changed only recorder wording while explicitly leaving the asserter definition broad.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/condition/structuredefinition-Condition.xml already conveys the FHIR-7855 meaning, adjusted only for later approved non-person asserters, and source/condition/condition-notes.xml already contains the Provenance usage note and nurse/physician example.
